{
  "checks_performed": [
    "Read only the authorized source JSON and draft JSON; used no web resources or other source files.",
    "Compared the exact target independently with the draft's final writeup and claimed resolution.",
    "Re-derived the Cayley connection sets, character counts, conference-matrix identity, Fourier LP, projection normalization, and Jacobi-sum eigenvalues.",
    "Checked the theta SDP dual, vertex-transitive product identity, induced-subgraph monotonicity, disjoint-union additivity, and all bound directions and algebra.",
    "Ran exact-arithmetic Fourier certificates for p=5,13,17 in check_small_prime_theta.py; all checks passed.",
    "Exhaustively enumerated all perfect matchings of K_17 in check_p17_matching.py using integer graph arithmetic; all checks passed."
  ],
  "claimed_resolution_verdict": "ACCURATE",
  "claims": [
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Writing Q for the nonzero squares and K_p=complement(H_p), both H_p and K_p are Cayley graphs on the multiplicative group Q. Their connection sets S and T have sizes (p−5)/4 and (p−1)/4, respectively.",
      "claim_sha256": "795ed33913c32d39fe2417fa65bc101e77faca81ce05cf48b6354cfdfb8aaca3",
      "evidence": "For x,y∈Q, χ(x−y)=χ(x/y−1), so adjacency depends only on x/y. The sets S={q≠1:χ(q−1)=1} and T={q≠1:χ(q−1)=−1} are inverse-closed. Moreover Σ_{q∈Q}χ(q−1)=−1, while |S|+|T|=|Q|−1=(p−3)/2. Hence |S|−|T|=−1 and the stated cardinalities follow.",
      "idx": 0,
      "search_method": "Direct quadratic-character calculation, including the exceptional point q=1",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "The localized Paley sign matrix B has operator norm at most √p, by an exact conference-matrix identity.",
      "claim_sha256": "c8308e04dc5141c9764b7a7152f80154092b8825a220bef787b950c52c04a437",
      "evidence": "For C_{xy}=χ(x−y), character correlation gives C²=pI−J. Ordering the vertices as {0}, Q, and {ν/q:q∈Q} for a nonsquare ν gives the stated blocks and, from the Q,Q block, B²+D²=pI−2J. Thus ||Bv||²+||Dv||²=p||v||²−2(1ᵀv)²≤p||v||², proving ||B||op≤√p.",
      "idx": 1,
      "search_method": "Exact block-matrix multiplication and character correlation",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "θ(K_p) is exactly an explicit finite Fourier linear program, or equivalently a nonnegative-vector problem for a half-dimensional Fourier projection.",
      "claim_sha256": "dbe7091a0bfcc58f921ae272454d59698db5250149564829537f94506a7c8119",
      "evidence": "Averaging over Q makes X_{xy}=f(x⁻¹y)/n. Trace, edge-zero, symmetry, and PSD become f(1)=1, f|_T=0, f(q)=f(q⁻¹), and nonnegative Fourier coefficients; the objective is Σ_qf(q). With y_ψ=hat f(ψ)/n, one has y≥0, Σy=1, and θ(K_p)=ny_triv. Fourier conjugation maps functions supported on D={1}∪S, whose size is n/2, onto the range of the rank-n/2 orthogonal projector P_D. Including the required conjugate-coordinate identification gives the claimed exact equivalence.",
      "idx": 2,
      "search_method": "Direct symmetry reduction and finite-group Fourier diagonalization of the theta SDP",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Every nontrivial Fourier eigenvalue of B is the real part of a Jacobi sum of modulus √p.",
      "claim_sha256": "fb0e1f3459459b08789c8ff83c29f295b16fac6da94de426672a97f3ac456068",
      "evidence": "For nontrivial ψ on Q and either extension A to F_p*, the eigenvalue is R_ψ=[J(A,χ)+J(Aχ,χ)]/2. Nontriviality of ψ excludes all exceptional characters: A and Aχ are both nontrivial and neither equals χ. Gauss-sum identities therefore give modulus √p for both Jacobi sums and product G(χ)²=p. They are conjugates, so R_ψ=Re J(A,χ).",
      "idx": 3,
      "search_method": "Jacobi-sum expansion with explicit checking of exceptional-character cases",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "For every vertex-transitive graph G on n vertices, θ(G)θ(complement(G))=n.",
      "claim_sha256": "c0d25350db9b4a8883cabcbb0a120a6665d7dfc3a72c577ae95eab63597356bb",
      "evidence": "The theta dual is min t with tI+Z−J PSD and Z supported on edges. Any dual certificate for G yields a primal certificate for its complement with value at least n/t, proving the product is at least n. Averaging an optimal primal X over a transitive automorphism group gives diag(X)=1/n and X1=(θ(G)/n)1. Then (n²/θ(G))X−J is PSD and is a complement-dual certificate with value n/θ(G), proving the reverse inequality.",
      "idx": 4,
      "search_method": "Primal-dual SDP proof with automorphism averaging",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Theta is monotone under taking induced subgraphs.",
      "claim_sha256": "56b84bbf6bde7b77fa333f818deeb52e18f30fec1578b4edd5d012576e053b1e",
      "evidence": "Zero-padding any feasible matrix for an induced subgraph preserves positive semidefiniteness, trace one, every edge-zero constraint, and the objective. Therefore its optimum cannot exceed that of the full graph.",
      "idx": 5,
      "search_method": "Direct feasible-solution embedding",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Theta is additive on disjoint unions: θ(G⊔L)=θ(G)+θ(L).",
      "claim_sha256": "3ac66b5dd218d8c2f9c49ef94fdfb9a24963b17ed8d60b26653a39bc46c97ba1",
      "evidence": "In Gram form, align the two optimal vector sums and allocate trace in proportion to θ(G),θ(L), attaining their sum. Conversely, if the two block traces are a,b, their vector-sum norms are at most √(aθ(G)) and √(bθ(L)); Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the total squared norm by (a+b)(θ(G)+θ(L))=θ(G)+θ(L).",
      "idx": 6,
      "search_method": "Two-sided Gram-representation argument",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "The full Paley graph P_p satisfies θ(P_p)=√p.",
      "claim_sha256": "4faa4108b8422c8eed33f4c31a2afb7948ff4b50b44f555906999b362cf01ca9",
      "evidence": "Translations act transitively on P_p, while multiplication by a nonsquare is an isomorphism from P_p to its complement. Applying the verified vertex-transitive product identity gives θ(P_p)²=p; positivity selects √p.",
      "idx": 7,
      "search_method": "Graph automorphisms followed by the theta product identity",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "For every eligible prime, θ(K_p)≤√p−1.",
      "claim_sha256": "f28e617fd4a43b327dbffc8cfa89f47b00b58a73cf137d085d372ab8f4f14d2e",
      "evidence": "Multiplication by a nonsquare identifies K_p with the Paley subgraph induced by the nonsquares N. Since −1 is a square, vertex 0 has no Paley neighbor in N. Thus P_p[{0}∪N] is an isolated vertex disjoint-unioned with K_p. Induced monotonicity and additivity give 1+θ(K_p)≤θ(P_p)=√p.",
      "idx": 8,
      "search_method": "Explicit induced-subgraph identification and theta graph operations",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "For every eligible prime, θ(H_p)≤(√p+1)²/(√p+3).",
      "claim_sha256": "f6f94fde213ed73705cc5b7c40061da565c64c8cd0b3a3517c0e8d7d6c579a6c",
      "evidence": "On 1⊥, A(H_p)=(B−I)/2, so every eigenvalue is at least −a with a=(√p+1)/2. For n=(p−1)/2 and d=(p−5)/4, the dual matrix tI+cA−J with c=n/(d+a) and t=na/(d+a) is PSD: it vanishes on 1 and has eigenvalues n(λ+a)/(d+a)≥0 on 1⊥. Algebra gives t=(√p+1)²/(√p+3), including p=5.",
      "idx": 9,
      "search_method": "Exact spectral theta-dual certificate",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "The unconditional two-sided bound is ((√p−1)(√p+3))/(2(√p+1))≤θ(K_p)≤√p−1.",
      "claim_sha256": "0ef947e6f216065adee76b97407c6a7e42ca67debedd298e3f7823a6ee1e5da2",
      "evidence": "The upper bound is claim 8. Since H_p is a Cayley graph and hence vertex-transitive, θ(H_p)θ(K_p)=n. Dividing n=(p−1)/2 by the verified upper bound on θ(H_p) yields exactly (√p−1)(√p+3)/(2(√p+1)).",
      "idx": 10,
      "search_method": "Combination of the two verified bounds with exact symbolic simplification",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "The proven bounds imply 1/√2≤liminf θ(K_p)/√(p/2)≤limsup θ(K_p)/√(p/2)≤√2, and isolate the unresolved step as asymptotic balance of the complementary theta numbers.",
      "claim_sha256": "33a22e55b9cf4e475c3d94b6f63c64494dbfcefc707afb1280c9a3b7e15d63c4",
      "evidence": "Dividing claim 10 by √p/√2 gives limiting endpoint constants 1/√2 and √2. Also n/(p/2)→1 and θ(H_p)θ(K_p)=n, so θ(K_p)/√(p/2)→1 is equivalent to both complementary theta numbers being asymptotic to √n, equivalently to their difference being o(√p). The bounds alone do not force this.",
      "idx": 11,
      "search_method": "Exact asymptotic normalization and use of the product identity",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_exploratory_unbiased_v2r3_scratch/explore_paley_localization_theta/audit-revision/plain/iter_2/check_small_prime_theta.py",
      "claim": "The exact small-prime values are θ(K_5)=1, θ(K_13)=2, θ(K_17)=8−4√2; correspondingly θ(H_5)=2, θ(H_13)=3, and θ(H_17)=2+√2.",
      "claim_sha256": "6f5530781cecf2924735d9828497739e442aef4d375a45c96b8ff2ebcccbc347",
      "evidence": "The exact checker verifies the connection sets and the Fourier primal and upper certificates. For p=13, a=1/2 is feasible and the l=3 inequality proves optimality. For p=17, a=2−√2 and b=3−2√2 are feasible; a positive exact combination of the l=3 and l=4 inequalities proves the matching upper bound. The complementary values follow exactly from product n. The checker passed without floating-point decisions.",
      "idx": 12,
      "search_method": "Exact rational and quadratic-field certificate evaluation",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "p=5 gives the empty graph and K_2; p=13 uses a=1/2; p=17 uses (a,b)=(2−√2,3−2√2)"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_exploratory_unbiased_v2r3_scratch/explore_paley_localization_theta/audit-revision/plain/iter_2/check_p17_matching.py",
      "claim": "A tempting exact explanation—K_p being a relabelled copy of H_p with one perfect matching added—is already false for p=17.",
      "claim_sha256": "4e630b87155ca9795181038a6d4b93f92796582b56680422340409d189a247ed",
      "evidence": "Exact exhaustive enumeration finds 14 perfect matchings in K_17. After deletion, 12 resulting graphs contain a triangle, whereas H_17 is triangle-free. The other two deletions each have six induced 4-cycles, whereas H_17 has four. Hence no deletion is isomorphic to H_17. The checker passed using integer graph arithmetic.",
      "idx": 13,
      "search_method": "Exhaustive enumeration of all perfect matchings and exact isomorphism invariants",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "p=17 with H_17=Cay(Z/8Z,{±1,4}) and K_17=Cay(Z/8Z,{±2,±3})"
    }
  ],
  "complete": true,
  "confirmed_refutations": [],
  "iteration": 2,
  "overall": "VERIFIED",
  "parent_sha256": "883cc72bd1a4f91e6cd39b6ec25b03ea70af53f3a60e555e2e15932f04ccc52d",

The draft proves only constant-factor bounds with limiting interval [1/√2,√2], plus exact reductions and reformulations. Those results permit both the target limit and alternatives, so they do not resolve the requested dichotomy. They are nevertheless correct and material partial progress. The final writeup explicitly says that it does not prove the requested limit, and claimed_resolution is PARTIAL; therefore the coverage claim is accurate rather than overstated.",
  "target_verdict": "VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS",
  "arm": "plain"
